stem.en: Two group-A parents have a group-O child. Kabir says "impossible, both parents are A". What are the parents' genotypes?

text.en: Both are AO. Each gives O half the time, and an OO child, group O, is one in four. Group A hides an O allele the way round hides wrinkled.
Impossible; the child is not theirs.

feedback.en: A is a phenotype. AO is a genotype that shows A and carries O. Two AO parents give O children a quarter of the time.

text.en: One parent must secretly be group O.

feedback.en: A group-O parent has no A allele and would test as O. These parents test as A and carry O as well.

text.en: The child's group will change to A as it grows.

feedback.en: Blood group is set by the alleles and does not change.

explanation.en: Work back from the recessive child. OO needs an O from each parent. Each group-A parent must be AO.
